newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures post large daily gains.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures post large daily gains.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures posted large daily gains on strength carried over from Friday's advance and support that spilled over from a resilient U.S. Treasury market.
Stock index futures ground their way upward much of the session, tracking moves in T-bond futures as they recovered from midmorning erosion and finished moderately higher and hugging session peaks.
Gains in over-the-counter stocks and key blue-chip issues, coupled with technical buying, attracted buyers to September Standard & Poor's (S&P) 500s as well, traders said.

Futures hit their peaks late in the session, although traders said afternoon volume stayed fairly light. The price boards on the Chicago Mercantile Exchange's trading floor showed estimated turnover in September S&P 500s of roughly 77,000 contracts.
"I think the bond close (helped)," said a S&P 500 futures floor broker. "They were weak early and then showed strength."
Traders said sizable buying from a couple of dealers helped underpin the contract, which cleared several resistance levels and periodically hit buystops.

They also noted some signs of hedge-fund shortcovering and early arbitrage buy programs before the Dow 30 industrials climbed more than 50 points and triggered the New York Stock Exchange's curb on computer-assisted program trades.
Blended fair value on Monday in nearby S&P 500s stood at roughly 0.40 point over cash. Arb buy programs needed at least 1.00 point premium, brokers said.

The ability of September S&P 500s to hurdle the 100-day moving average at 662.50 impressed some technicians. But the contract then rammed into a ceiling at 665.20, which one floor chartist said constituted an 11-month trendline.
Rolling continued into December S&P 500s futures and out of September, which stops trading on September 19.
September Nikkei 225 index futures pared early losses on buying from a commission house and a French bank affiliate that one floor broker estimated at 2,000 contracts each.
But the contract stalled below resistance near 20,500.00, although its narrow premium over the Asian market could mean slightly more upside, the broker added.

Sept S&P 500s jumped 6.80 pts to 665.05, Midcap 400s up 0.45 pt at 233.00, Value Lines gained 2.20 pts to 622.00, NYSE Composite rose 3.05 to 356.80, Nikkei lost 75.0 to 20,325.0. --Derivatives Desk 312-408-8750 E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
